rules.rule_name: Prohibition of Proprietary Brand Names in Tender Specifications
rules.authority: CVC Office Memorandum No. 03-05-1-CTE-9 / GFR 2017 Rule 144(vii) & Rule 157
rules.message: Specific brand names without generic technical performance parameters qualify as tender tailoring under CVC anti-corruption guidelines.
rules.recommended_action: Strip proprietary brand names. Replace with generic functional parameters and relevant Indian Standard (IS) with 'or equivalent certified to IS'.

rules.rule_name: Citation of Obsolete, Superseded, or Withdrawn BIS Standards
rules.message: Citing obsolete revisions restricts bidder participation and violates statutory public procurement quality mandates.
rules.recommended_action: Update standard to the latest active revision and ensure compliance with all gazetted amendments.

rules.rule_name: Foreign Standards Cited Without National Equivalence Clause
rules.authority: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017 & GFR Rule 144(vii)
rules.message: Mandating foreign standards when national standards exist unfairly discriminates against domestic Indian manufacturers and violates GFR 144(vii).
rules.recommended_action: Convert foreign standard to the harmonized Indian Standard (IS) equivalent.

rules.rule_name: Excessive or Tailored Financial / Technical Pre-Qualification Criteria
rules.message: Disproportionate financial turnover or restrictive single-vendor eligibility conditions unduly restrict fair competition.
rules.recommended_action: Align turnover criteria with CVC formula (typically 30% to 50% of estimated annual tender value).

rules.rule_name: Missing Mandatory BIS Quality Control Order (QCO) Statutory Clause
rules.authority: Section 16 of the BIS Act, 2016 & Respective Ministry QCO Gazettes
rules.message: Procuring items governed by mandatory QCOs without compulsory BIS certification is a criminal regulatory offense under the BIS Act, 2016.
rules.recommended_action: Insert mandatory clause: 'The supplied goods must bear valid BIS Standard Mark (ISI mark / CRS) and the bidder must hold a valid BIS license on the date of bid submission.'
